Hi Andrew,

Hal here, I look after the hardware side at HeliumDeploy. Two things in your message, so let me take them one at a time.

The plug first. The BC04 ships with a power supply that takes a standard IEC lead, so the "kettle cable" you used is exactly the right part and it is safe to keep using as long as it is a normal fused UK lead. You should not have had to find one yourself, so I have asked the team to send you a proper UK cord for it, and a colleague is picking that up today and will confirm it to you.

Now Harlo OS. It does not come pre installed on the BC04, it is free firmware you flash yourself and it takes about two minutes, so nothing is missing from your unit. The flasher runs in the browser at harlolabs.com, in Chrome or Edge on a desktop or laptop, and the way it is meant to go is: take the display module off the miner, or use the USB C port directly, connect it to the computer, pick your model profile, choose the factory image since this is the first time, then erase and install and power the unit up again.

On the error you are seeing when you connect the LilyGo module, I do not want to guess at it. I have not been able to match that exact wording to a known Harlo OS message, and a made up answer helps nobody. What I can tell you is what causes nearly every failed connect at that step, in the order worth trying. One, the USB cable: most spare USB C cables are charge only and will never enumerate, so use a known data cable, ideally the one that came with a phone or a hard drive you have synced with. Two, the port being held by something else: close every other browser tab with the flasher open, and close Arduino IDE, any serial monitor or any vendor flashing tool, then unplug and replug. Three, the port itself: plug straight into the computer, not through a hub or a monitor. Four, if it connects but then fails to initialise, hold the BOOT button on the module while you plug it in, keep holding it, then click install. Five, make sure you have picked the BC04 profile and not another Hammer model. That last one matters more than it looks: the BC01 and BC04 boards do not share the same ASIC wiring, so the wrong image leaves a miner that boots and shows a web page but never returns a single share, and it reads as dead hardware when it is not.

If you can send me a screenshot of the error exactly as it appears, plus the firmware version the miner shows in its web interface today, I will tell you precisely what it is rather than what it probably is. In the meantime the miner will mine perfectly well on the firmware it shipped with, so nothing is lost while we sort this.

I have also passed this to JD, who writes Harlo OS himself. The fastest route to him is the Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf , where he is @nullhashrate and answers most days.

Sorry again for the run you have had with this order.

Hal, HeliumDeploy technical support

Hi Andrew,

Good, that settles two things. A thick 13A fused lead is exactly right, and a BC04 that is up and mining means the board, the regulator and the power side are all healthy. Nothing is wrong with the miner itself, this is purely a flashing problem on the PC side.

Before you spend tomorrow on cables, one thing that will save you the trip: the phone will not work. The browser flasher uses Web Serial, which only exists in Chrome and Edge on a desktop or laptop. Chrome on Android and anything on an iPhone will not see the module at all, so keep it to the PC.

Since both your leads are known data cables, the cable is probably not the fault, and there is a quick way to prove it. Open Device Manager on the PC, expand Ports (COM and LPT) and also Universal Serial Bus devices, then plug the LilyGo module in on its own with the miner unplugged from the mains. If a new entry appears when you connect and disappears when you unplug, the cable and the port are fine and the problem is further along. If nothing appears at all with either lead, it is the cable or the USB port, and then a different lead or a different port on the back of the PC is the fix. Use a port directly on the machine, not a hub, a monitor or a keyboard.

If the module does show up but the install still fails, put it into boot mode by hand. Hold the BOOT button on the LilyGo, keep holding it while you plug the USB in, then let go and click install in the flasher. That one step clears most failed connects on these ESP32 S3 modules.

When you do get the error again, send me the whole screen rather than just the code, and tell me two things with it: whether anything appeared in Device Manager when you plugged in, and which model profile you selected in the flasher. With those I can tell you exactly what it is. I will not guess at the wording, because the wrong meaning sends you down the wrong path.

JD, who writes Harlo OS, already has this from me. If you want him directly, he is @nullhashrate on our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf and he is in there most days. The UK cord is with a colleague and they will confirm that to you.

Take your time, the miner is earning in the meantime.

Hal, HeliumDeploy technical support
Searched the web · LilyGo T-Display-S3 BOOT button which side of USB-C RST IO0

Hi Andrew,

That is good news. COM3 appearing in Device Manager when you plug the module in proves the cable and the USB port are fine, so you can stop testing leads. Whatever the error is, it happens after the connection is made, not because of it.

On the BOOT button. The two little buttons sit on the same edge as the USB C socket, one either side of it, and on these LilyGo modules they are rarely labelled in a way you can read once the board is in a case. The simple way to tell them apart is to power the module up and press one of them briefly on its own. The one that makes the screen blank and restart is RST. The other one, by elimination, is BOOT. That test costs you nothing and it is safe to do.

Once you know which is which, the proper download mode sequence for this module is: with the USB cable connected, press and hold BOOT, then press and release RST while still holding BOOT, then let go of BOOT. The screen will usually stay dark or blank at that point, which is correct, that is the board sitting in the ROM bootloader waiting. Now go to the flasher page, click install, and in the popup pick the COM3 entry. It should get through the connect step this time.

Two small things that catch people at that popup. If Chrome lists more than one port, pick COM3 and nothing else, and make sure no other tab with the flasher open and no serial monitor or Arduino window is running in the background, because whichever one grabbed the port first keeps it. After a failed attempt, unplug the module for five seconds and redo the BOOT and RST sequence from scratch rather than clicking install again straight away.

If it still stops, send me a photo or screenshot of the popup and the error exactly as it appears on screen, plus the model profile you picked in the flasher. I would rather read the real wording than tell you what I think it probably means. I will have an answer for you from that.

JD, who writes Harlo OS, is @nullhashrate on our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf and that is the quickest route if you want a live pair of eyes while you have the module in your hand.

The UK cord is already with the team. They are offline overnight and pick it up today from 10am Eastern, and the confirmation will come to you by email.

Your miner carries on earning on the stock firmware in the meantime, so there is no rush on this.

Hal, HeliumDeploy technical support

Hi Andrew,

Thanks for working through that. You have now ruled out the three usual suspects, so we stop guessing and get the error itself in front of the person who wrote the software.

Two things I still need from you, and they are quick. First, a photo or screenshot of the error exactly as it appears, the whole window rather than just the code. I have deliberately not told you what it means because I cannot match that wording to anything I can verify for this model, and a wrong meaning would send you further down the wrong path. Second, tell me which model profile you selected on the flasher page before the error appeared.

While you are at it, one thing we have not checked. Was the miner itself unplugged from the mains with the display module taken off it, or was the module still attached to a powered BC04 when you connected the USB? If the module is still sitting on a live miner, it has two power sources fighting each other and the flash can fail exactly like this. Switch the miner off at the wall, unplug it, take the display module off, then connect only the USB cable to the PC and try the install again. That one is worth a try before anything else.

Beyond that there are two cheap experiments if you have the means. Try Edge rather than Chrome on the same PC, and if you have a second computer, try that, because the fault can sit in a driver or a security tool on one machine. Neither is likely to be the answer, but both are free.

I have passed the whole history to JD, who writes Harlo OS himself. The team is offline overnight and picks this up today from 10am Eastern, and the answer will come to you by email. If you would rather not wait, he is @nullhashrate on our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf and you can show him the error live with the module in your hand, which is by far the fastest route.

Nothing here is a fault with your miner. It is running and earning on its factory firmware, and Harlo OS can go on it whenever we crack this.

Hal, HeliumDeploy technical support
